title: Land Record and KCC Loan Document Extraction
summary: Read Khatauni, 7/12, Jamabandi and other land records plus KCC loan papers, extract holdings and crops, convert local area units, and flag mismatches before a credit officer sanctions.

seo.title: Land Record and KCC Document Extraction | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads land records such as Khatauni, 7/12 and Jamabandi plus KCC loan files, converts local units and flags mismatches for credit officers.

problem.intro: A Kisan Credit Card or crop loan file depends on land records that look different in every state: a Khatauni in Uttar Pradesh, a 7/12 extract in Maharashtra, a Jamabandi in Punjab or Rajasthan, an RTC in Karnataka. Credit staff read these by hand, convert bighas and gunthas to acres, and check owner names against KYC before they can assess the loan.

pain_points.title: State-by-state formats
pain_points.detail: Each state's record has its own layout, language and terms, so one checklist does not fit every branch.

pain_points.title: Local area units
pain_points.detail: Holdings appear in bigha, biswa, guntha, kanal or hectare, and the size of a bigha differs between states and even districts.

pain_points.title: Name and share mismatches
pain_points.detail: Joint holdings, transliterated names and inherited shares make it hard to confirm how much land the applicant actually holds.

pain_points.title: Missed charges and mutations
pain_points.detail: Existing bank charges, pending mutations and other lenders' entries in the record are easy to overlook under volume.

solution.overview: We build a document pipeline for agri-loan files. It accepts scanned or downloaded land records and KCC application documents, identifies the state format, and extracts owner names, survey or khasra numbers, holding area, share, crop and any recorded charge or mutation. Area is converted to a standard unit using a district-level unit table your credit team approves. Names are matched against KYC with transliteration-aware comparison. The pipeline compares the holding and declared crops with the scale of finance used to size the limit, and flags gaps. Credit officers see every extracted value next to its source text, and any low-confidence field or failed check goes to them for confirmation.
capabilities: Recognises common state land record formats and local-language text
Extracts owner, share, survey or khasra number, area, crop and charge entries
Converts bigha, guntha, kanal and other units using an approved district table
Transliteration-aware name matching against KYC documents
Checks holding and crops against scale of finance inputs
Source-linked review screen for credit officers

workflow.title: Collect the loan file
workflow.detail: Land records, KCC application, KYC and no-dues certificates arrive from the branch, a field agent app or a permitted portal download.

workflow.title: Identify and extract
workflow.detail: Each document is classified by type and state format, and fields are extracted with a confidence score.

workflow.title: Normalise units and names
workflow.detail: Area is converted to a standard unit and names are matched across land record and KYC.

workflow.title: Run credit checks
workflow.detail: The pipeline checks holdings, shares, charges and crops against the application and scale of finance.

workflow.title: Credit officer review
workflow.detail: Low-confidence fields and failed checks go to the credit officer with the source text highlighted.

workflow.title: Send to the loan system
workflow.detail: Structured data and the review trail are pushed to the loan origination system for sanction.

inputs: Land records such as Khatauni, 7/12 extract, Jamabandi, RTC or Patta
KCC or crop loan application form
Scale of finance table for the district and crop
outputs: Structured holding record with owners, shares, survey numbers and area in a standard unit
Flags for charges, mutations and shortfalls against the requested limit
Audit trail of extraction and edits
human_in_the_loop: Credit officers confirm low-confidence fields, resolve name and share mismatches, and decide on every flagged charge or mutation. Sanction decisions stay entirely with the lender.
integrations: Loan origination system via API or staging table
State land record portals, where access is permitted
guardrails: Unit conversion only from a table approved by the credit team, with district overrides
Masked Aadhaar only; full numbers never stored
Every value linked to its source text
Periodic re-check of auto-cleared files by credit audit
compliance_notes: Supports the documentation and audit trail lenders keep under RBI directions on the Kisan Credit Card scheme.
Aadhaar is handled in masked form per UIDAI rules, and personal data in line with the DPDP Act 2023.

faqs.q: Which states' land records can it read?
faqs.a: We start with the state formats that make up most of your book and add others one at a time. Each new format is tested on real samples before it is switched on.

faqs.q: Can it fetch records from state portals?
faqs.a: Where your institution has permitted access, the pipeline can take portal downloads directly. Otherwise it works from scans or files uploaded by branches and field agents.

faqs.q: How does it handle handwritten mutation entries?
faqs.a: Handwritten entries are extracted where legible, and anything uncertain goes to the credit officer instead of being guessed. The pilot report shows handwritten and printed accuracy separately.

faqs.q: Does the AI decide the loan amount?
faqs.a: No. It prepares checked data and flags gaps against the scale of finance. The credit officer and your sanctioning authority decide the limit.
